content: Sodium bicarbonate is an antacid that is prescribed to alleviate symptoms of heartburn and acid indigestion. Additionally, your doctor may recommend sodium bicarbonate to reduce the acidity of your blood or urine in specific medical conditions. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Sodium bicarbonate is available in tablet and powder forms for oral administration. The frequency of use ranges from one to four times daily, depending on the condition being treated. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take sodium bicarbonate exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. If you are using sodium bicarbonate as an antacid, it should be taken 1 to 2 hours after meals with a full glass of water. For other indications, it may be taken with or without food. Avoid taking sodium bicarbonate on an overly full stomach. If using the powdered form, dissolve it in at least 4 ounces of water and measure the dose accurately with a measuring spoon. Do not use sodium bicarbonate for more than two weeks unless instructed by your doctor. If your symptoms do not improve, contact your doctor. Sodium bicarbonate should not be given to children under 12 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before taking sodium bicarbonate, inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially other antacids, aspirin or aspirin-like drugs, benzodiazepines, flecainide (Tambocor), iron supplements, ketoconazole (Nizoral), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), methenamine (Hiprex, Urex), methotrexate, quinidine, sulfa-containing antibiotics, tetracycline (Sumycin), or vitamins. Sodium bicarbonate should be taken at least two hours apart from other medications. Inform your doctor if you have a history of high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, kidney disease, or recent gastrointestinal bleeding. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking sodium bicarbonate, notify your doctor immediately. This medication increases sodium levels in the body. If you are on a sodium-restricted diet, consult your doctor before using sodium bicarbonate. If you miss a dose and are on a specific schedule, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Sodium bicarbonate may cause mild side effects such as increased thirst, stomach cramps, or gas. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include severe headache, upset stomach, vomiting that resembles coffee grounds, loss of appetite, irritability, weakness, frequent urination, slow breathing, swelling of the feet or lower legs, bloody or black stools, or blood in the urine. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, stop taking sodium bicarbonate and contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store sodium bicarbonate in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If your doctor has prescribed sodium bicarbonate, ensure you attend all scheduled appointments to monitor your response to the medication.
